title: The UGC-NET June 2024 Cancellation Case
dek: A day after over 9 lakh candidates sat India's national eligibility test for university teaching and PhD admission, a cyber-crime unit flagged that the question paper had surfaced for sale on the darknet — forcing an unprecedented last-minute cancellation and a CBI probe.

heroStat.label: candidates who had already sat the UGC-NET June 2024 exam before it was cancelled a day later over darknet-leak concerns

promise.quote: The UGC-NET examination will be conducted with full transparency and sanctity, on the basis of a question paper that remains secure until the test itself.
promise.madeBy: National Testing Agency (NTA) and Ministry of Education, Government of India
promise.role: Central agency and ministry responsible for conducting UGC-NET, the eligibility test for Junior Research Fellowships, assistant professorships, and PhD admission
promise.context: This reflects the NTA and Ministry's standard institutional mandate for UGC-NET June 2024, rather than a verified quotation from a specific official statement, which this entry has not located.

target.description: A national eligibility exam, conducted in a single day for 83 subjects across 317 exam cities, on the basis of a question paper kept confidential until the scheduled test time for each candidate.
target.standard: NTA's own examination-security protocols, applied nationally just weeks after the NEET-UG 2024 leak (covered separately on this site) had already drawn scrutiny to the agency.

reality.description: NTA conducted UGC-NET June 2024 in pen-and-paper mode on 18 June 2024 for 83 subjects across 317 cities; of over 11.21 lakh registered candidates, around 9.08 lakh appeared. On 19 June 2024, the Ministry of Education said it had received inputs from the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre's (I4C) National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit, under the Home Ministry, indicating the exam's integrity 'may have been compromised' — reported by officials, including Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, as the question paper having surfaced for sale on the darknet. The Ministry cancelled the already-conducted exam that same evening and referred the matter to the CBI, which registered a case against unknown persons. NTA rescheduled and conducted the exam in computer-based mode between 21 August and 4 September 2024. This entry has not confirmed any arrests, chargesheets, or the CBI investigation's outcome.

gap.metricLabel: Candidates who had already completed the exam vs. hours before the government cancelled it over the darknet-leak report
gap.note: The exam was cancelled not before or during the test, but roughly a day after nearly a million candidates had already completed it — underscoring that the security failure was detected only after the fact, via a cyber-crime unit's monitoring rather than NTA's own exam-day controls.
